C-AUDIT-SCORING-V3.Summary: Scoring version 3: bound the total deduction of medium findings and apply the per-audit band caps to the overall score, so a more thorough audit can no longer score lower than a shallow one and a confirmed critical or high finding can no longer hide behind clean audits.
C-AUDIT-SCORING-V3.Problem: Two calibration defects, both shown by real full-profile runs and both acknowledged in the change journal as open. First, medium findings have no aggregate limit: a run with one high and six medium findings scored 35 ("poor") for a test suite that an independent reference rated 83, because every medium beyond the first five kept deducting 6 points — the more carefully the audit looks, the lower the score, which punishes thoroughness. Second, the overall score is an unbounded mean of audit scores: a repository with a confirmed critical finding in one audit and clean results in the other four would average 80 and read "good", although the per-audit formula states that a confirmed critical always lands in the poor band. The formula's own band promises are broken at the aggregate level.

Goals.Goal: Medium findings together deduct at most 30 points in one audit, in addition to the existing 14-point limit for low findings.

The overall score inherits the per-audit caps: if any audit that ran has a counted critical finding, the overall score is at most 39; otherwise, if any audit has a counted high finding, the overall score is at most 69.
Counting rules (which findings are counted) stay exactly as in scoring version 2.
SCORING_VERSION becomes 3; the score calculation shown in reports renders the new limits and caps as explicit steps.
reference/scoring.md documents version 3: the formula, why 30 and why the overall caps, and updated band meanings.
CLI tests on node:test cover both limits with synthetic fixtures, including the determinism check (same findings scored twice give the same score).

Constraints.Constraint: Weights stay 40/15/6/2 and deductions stay linear apart from the aggregate limits; no severity re-weighting.
Band thresholds stay 0-39 poor, 40-69 fair, 70-100 good; only their wording may change to match the new reachable combinations.
The formula stays implementable as deterministic arithmetic recomputable by hand from the findings list; the report prints every step.
Scores are comparable only within the same scoring version; report and diff surface a version difference, as they already do for rubric versions.
Test fixtures are synthetic; no findings or numbers from audits of private repositories enter this repository.
Only skills/smart-audit CLI scoring, its tests, and its scoring reference change; rubrics, agents, schemas, and the review skill are untouched.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Density-based or per-surface scoring; criteria-weighted scores.
Changing severity weights, confidence handling, accepted-risks rules, or band thresholds.
Migrating or rescoring runs recorded under earlier scoring versions; recorded runs keep their recorded score and version.
Rubric changes, recall improvements, or cross-run coverage accounting (tracked separately as deferred directions).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A synthetic findings document with ten counted medium findings and nothing else deducts exactly 30 points; the eleventh medium changes nothing.

A synthetic run with four clean audits (100 each) and one audit holding a counted critical finding yields an overall score of at most 39; the same run with a counted high instead of the critical yields at most 69.
A mixed fixture reproducing the ladder property: one high finding still outweighs any number of medium findings and the 14-point low limit.
Scoring the same findings file twice produces the same score and identical file content.
report renders the medium limit and each applied cap as named steps of the calculation.
Comparing runs with different scoring versions emits the existing version-mismatch note, under a node:test.
make validate and make test pass; existing tests are updated for version 3 expectations rather than deleted.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: node:test suites for score and report show the new limit and cap cases green with the rule names asserted; determinism test unchanged and green; no fixture references a private repository.

Assumptions.Assumption: The medium limit of 30 is chosen so that medium findings alone can never push a score out of the good band (100 - 30 = 70), matching the existing choice of 14 for low findings (100 - 14 = 86, less than one high finding's weight).
The overall caps reuse the per-audit cap values, so the reader can state one rule at both levels: a counted critical means poor, a counted high can never be good.
Calibration feedback beyond these two defects (recall, coverage accounting, blind-run validation) is deferred by the maintainer to later changes.
